title: Microsoft has a new machine learning tool to improve weather forecasts
key_facts: Microsoft researchers published a method in Nature on 14 Oct 2026 for more accurate weather forecasts two to six weeks ahead.
The method, Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC), uses machine learning to correct systematic bias in existing forecast models rather than building a new model.
It improved the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) physics-based model for 98 percent of precipitation and 92 percent of temperature targets.
It doubled the accuracy of ECMWF's new AI forecasting system in the study's analysis.
It runs on CPUs and is released as open-source software.
Matthew Chantry of ECMWF said turning ideas into an operational process is the hardest step.
Rhiza Research is testing PBC with the Kenya Meteorological Service Authority, funded by the Gates Foundation.
quote_evidence: Researchers with the company say they’ve found a new, cost-effective way to make more accurate weather forecasts two to six weeks in advance
“As always, turning ideas into reality [in] an operational process is a most challenging step,” Chantry added.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheap, CPU-only tool could bring better multi-week forecasts to resource-limited weather agencies.
notes: Results are the authors' own, published in Nature; not yet operational.
